dominant_strengths: Confident display type with tight tracking and a clean italic subtitle establishes a refined editorial tone.
Restrained dark palette with semantic dot colors (green/blue/yellow/red) reads instantly without overwhelming the surface.
Keyboard hint row with kbd-style chips signals craft and behavioral depth beyond a standard demo.
dominant_weaknesses: Composition is inert — centered stack with huge empty canvas above and below, no toast preview visible in the static frame.
Buttons are generic rounded rectangles with weak hover affordance; the 2x2 grid plus full-width 'Fire all four' feels mechanical, not designed.
Nothing here is distinctive to toast notifications — could be any control panel; brief promises drag/hover/actions but none are demonstrated visually.
fix_priorities: Show a live toast stack in-frame (stacked, peeking, with progress ring) so the design demonstrates its own thesis.
Differentiate the four trigger buttons with tinted borders or subtle backgrounds matching their semantic dot color.
Tighten vertical rhythm — pull the title block up and anchor toasts to a corner to create real spatial tension.
Add a micro-illustration or annotated callouts for hover/drag/action behaviors to lift reflective value.
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral intent is strongest (keyboard shortcuts, semantic triggers), but visceral impact is muted by the empty canvas and reflective payoff is thin without visible toasts.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially fits — it's a launcher panel for toasts rather than an actual notification-stack design, so the 'improved stack' brief is asserted but not shown.
